text:
---

## Abstract

This investigation asked whether influenza virus data are present within records annotated as *E. coli* datasets in the NIAID Data Ecosystem (NDE). Two complementary queries were executed against the NDE API: (1) a facet count of `infectiousAgent.name` restricted to free-text matches on "E. coli" across 55,295 Dataset records, and (2) a co-occurrence query pairing "E. coli AND influenza" to inspect the 190 records where both terms appear together, along with a strict field-level filter (`infectiousAgent.name:influenza`) to test for direct annotation overlap. The facet of the 55,295 E. coli datasets returns no influenza virus entry in the top 50 infectious agents. The co-occurrence query of 190 records reveals *Haemophilus influenzae* (66 counts) — a gram-negative bacterium, not an influenza virus — as the only "influenza"-bearing agent alongside *E. coli*. A strict field filter for `infectiousAgent.name:influenza` within E. coli records returns zero hits. In summary, **no influenza virus data are embedded in E. coli records** in this ecosystem; the apparent overlap is entirely attributable to the bacterium *Haemophilus influenzae*, which shares the word "influenza" in its name.

---

## I. Introduction

**Background.** *Escherichia coli* is one of the most heavily studied model organisms in microbiology, accounting for tens of thousands of datasets in public repositories. Influenza viruses (family *Orthomyxoviridae*) are a completely unrelated group of RNA viruses responsible for seasonal and pandemic respiratory disease. Cross-contamination of metadata — where records for one organism inadvertently carry annotations belonging to another — is a known quality issue in federated data ecosystems. The question posed here is whether such contamination exists in this specific case.

**Literature Review.** No literature was retrieved for this query.

**Knowledge Gap.** Federated metadata indexing can introduce ambiguity when common English words appear in both pathogen names (e.g., *Haemophilus influenzae*) and virus family names (e.g., Influenza A virus). It was unclear whether NDE records tagged as "E. coli" datasets also carry influenza virus annotations.

**Objective & Hypothesis.** Objective: determine whether any NDE Dataset records annotated with *E. coli* also carry influenza virus as an infectious agent. Hypothesis: no such overlap exists, because these organisms occupy entirely different biological kingdoms and research contexts; any apparent co-occurrence will be attributable to the bacterium *H. influenzae*.

---

## II. Materials and Methods

**Study Design.** The NDE API was queried in two stages — first to characterize the infectious-agent landscape of E. coli records broadly, then to test specifically for influenza co-occurrence.

**Materials.**
- NIAID Data Ecosystem (NDE) API, accessed via the `nde_facet_counts` and `nde_raw_query` tools.

**Procedures.**

1. **Broad facet query** (`nde_facet_counts`): `query = "E. coli"`, `record_type = "Dataset"`, `fields = "infectiousAgent.name"`, `top_n = 50`. This returned the top 50 infectious agents annotated across all Dataset records matching "E. coli".

2. **Co-occurrence facet query** (`nde_facet_counts`): `query = "E. coli AND influenza"`, `record_type = "Dataset"`, `fields = "infectiousAgent.name"`, `top_n = 20`. This returned the infectious agents annotated in the 190 records where both terms appear.

3. **Strict field filter query** (`nde_raw_query`): `q = "E. coli AND infectiousAgent.name:influenza"`, `record_type = "Dataset"`, `size = 5`. This tested whether any record is simultaneously tagged with E. coli (free text) and influenza (as a structured `infectiousAgent.name` field value).

**Statistical Analysis.** All counts are raw document frequencies as returned by the NDE facet API. Percentages are not calculated, as the denominators differ between queries. No deduplication was performed beyond what NDE applies internally.

---

## III. Results

**Table 1. Top infectious agents in the 55,295 "E. coli" Dataset records (top 10 shown)**

| Rank | Infectious Agent | Count |
|------|-----------------|-------|
| 1 | *Escherichia coli* | 42,539 |
| 2 | *Escherichia coli* (strain K12) | 2,379 |
| 3 | *Klebsiella pneumoniae* | 1,632 |
| 4 | *Staphylococcus aureus* | 1,394 |
| 5 | *E. coli* str. K-12 substr. MG1655 | 1,087 |
| 6 | *Pseudomonas aeruginosa* | 990 |
| 7 | Bacterium | 752 |
| 8 | Synthetic construct | 530 |
| 9 | *Caenorhabditis elegans* | 487 |
| 10 | *Acinetobacter baumannii* | 459 |

No influenza virus appears in the top 50 agents.

**Table 2. Infectious agents in the 190 records matching "E. coli AND influenza" (top 10 shown)**

| Rank | Infectious Agent | Count |
|------|-----------------|-------|
| 1 | *Escherichia coli* | 143 |
| 2 | *Haemophilus influenzae* | 66 |
| 3 | *Staphylococcus aureus* | 43 |
| 4 | *Streptococcus pneumoniae* | 40 |
| 5 | *Klebsiella pneumoniae* | 33 |
| 6 | *Pseudomonas aeruginosa* | 32 |
| 7 | *Streptococcus pyogenes* | 23 |
| 8 | *Acinetobacter baumannii* | 21 |
| 9 | *Enterococcus faecalis* | 20 |
| 10 | *Proteus mirabilis* | 20 |

**Findings.** The strict field-level query (`infectiousAgent.name:influenza AND E. coli`) returned **0 records**. The word "influenza" in the co-occurrence query is matched entirely through *Haemophilus influenzae*, a bacterium. No influenza virus (e.g., Influenza A virus, Influenza B virus) appears in any structured field among E. coli Dataset records.

---

## IV. Discussion

**Interpretation.** The objective is met with a clear negative result: there are no influenza virus records embedded within E. coli-annotated datasets in NDE. The three queries converge on the same conclusion.

**Context.** The 190 co-occurrence records arise because the free-text term "influenza" matches the species name *Haemophilus influenzae*, which is a gram-negative bacterium frequently studied alongside *E. coli* in antibiotic resistance and respiratory infection contexts. This is a well-known naming artifact — *H. influenzae* was originally (incorrectly) thought to cause influenza, and the name persisted.

**Limitations.**
- The NDE free-text query "E. coli" matches any record containing that string in any field, including descriptions that mention E. coli as a comparison organism, not necessarily as the study subject.
- NDE record annotations depend on submitter-supplied metadata; records with no `infectiousAgent.name` field (5,129 in the broad query) cannot be characterized.
- This analysis covers only `Dataset` record types; `Sample` and other types were not queried and could in principle contain different patterns.
- NDE is a federated index; its completeness depends on the upstream repositories it ingests.

**Conclusion & Future Directions.** No influenza virus data exist within E. coli records in NDE. The apparent overlap is a linguistic artifact of the name *Haemophilus influenzae*. A logical next step would be to query `record_type = "Sample"` with the same filters to confirm the pattern holds at the sample level, or to audit multi-pathogen studies (e.g., co-infection datasets) where both organisms might legitimately co-occur.

---

## References

[1] NIAID Data Ecosystem (NDE) API — broad E. coli facet query:
`https://api.data.niaid.nih.gov/v1/query?q=%28E.+coli%29+AND+%40type%3A%22Dataset%22&size=0&facets=infectiousAgent.name&facet_size=50`

[2] NIAID Data Ecosystem (NDE) API — co-occurrence "E. coli AND influenza" facet query:
`https://api.data.niaid.nih.gov/v1/query?q=%28E.+coli+AND+influenza%29+AND+%40type%3A%22Dataset%22&size=0&facets=infectiousAgent.name&facet_size=20`

[3] NIAID Data Ecosystem (NDE) API — strict field filter query:
`https://api.data.niaid.nih.gov/v1/query?q=E.+coli+AND+infectiousAgent.name%3Ainfluenza&size=5&_source=_id%2C%40type%2Cname%2Cdescription%2Curl%2Cdoi%2Cidentifier%2Cdate%2CdatePublished%2CdateModified%2CincludedInDataCatalog.name%2CincludedInDataCatalog.url%2CincludedInDataCatalog.archivedAt%2Cauthor.name%2CinfectiousAgent.name%2CinfectiousAgent.displayName%2Cspecies.name%2ChealthCondition.name%2CmeasurementTechnique.name%2CtopicCategory.name%2Ckeywords%2CconditionsOfAccess%2Clicense%2Cdistribution.contentUrl%2CsourceOrganization.name%2Cfunding.funder.name%2CprogrammingLanguage%2CapplicationCategory%2CoperatingSystem%2CsoftwareVersion%2CcodeRepository%2CisBasedOn.identifier%2CvariableMeasured.name%2Cvalue%2CunitText%2CmarginOfError.name%2CmarginOfError.value%2CobservationAbout.name%2CobservationAbout.identifier%2CmeasuredProperty.name%2CobservationType.name%2CmeasurementQualifier%2CsubjectOf.identifier`
